summary: Completed comprehensive testing of CyberCopilote TPME diagnostic wizard flow, dashboard display, and action plan functionality. Identified critical localStorage persistence issue in diagnostic completion flow.

critical_bugs.issue: localStorage data not persisting during diagnostic completion flow
critical_bugs.impact: Prevents dashboard from showing results after completing diagnostic
critical_bugs.details: The diagnostic wizard progresses through all 16 questions correctly, but localStorage (diagnosticAnswers, scores, actionPlan, onboardingDone) is not being saved during the process. This causes the dashboard to show welcome screen instead of results.

integration_issues.issue: Data persistence failure prevents proper flow completion

passed_tests: Landing page loads correctly with French UI
Diagnostic wizard starts successfully from landing page
All 16 diagnostic questions display properly in French
Progress indicator shows correct question count (X/16)
Dashboard displays correctly when localStorage data is manually set
Score card shows cyber score (24/100) with severity badge (Risque Critique)
Quick stats display correctly (Terminees, A faire, Urgentes)
Category breakdown shows all 7 security categories with proper scores
Action plan page displays tasks grouped by period (today, week)
Task cards show proper information (title, time, impact, effort)
Task expansion reveals detailed explanation and step-by-step instructions
Task completion toggle works with visual feedback (checkmark, line-through)
Completion percentage updates correctly (0% → 33% after completing one task)
French language implementation throughout the application
action_item_for_main_agent: Fix critical localStorage persistence issue in diagnostic wizard completion flow. The handleFinish function in DiagnosticWizard.js is not properly saving data to localStorage, preventing the dashboard from displaying results after diagnostic completion. Verify that saveDiagnosticAnswers, saveScores, saveActionPlan, and setOnboardingDone functions are being called correctly.
